newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Swire hopes for faster China expansion.
newsitem.headline: Swire hopes for faster China expansion.

text.p: Swire Pacific Ltd said on Saturday it would like to develop its China business more rapidly in coming years, while at the same time avoiding "an unwisely rapid" rate of development there.
"I think probably my desire would be to see our businesses in China develop perhaps more quickly than they have done," chairman Peter Sutch told reporters on Saturday.

"I talked on many occasions about our wish to see the Swire Pac conglomerate a little bit more balanced - property and aviation at the moment is very dominant... In order to balance it we would have to throw a lot of money at it in a short period of time which is not our style," he added.

Sutch said Swire wanted to expand its current base on the mainland which involves beverage can and paint manufacturing and suger refining. Swire also distributes Reebok shoes and apparel and Volvo cars in Hong Kong and China.

While Swire's businesses on the mainland were not "quite as sexy as people want", Sutch said they were right for China's current stage of development. "They can actually be developed into a very big and profitable business," he said.

He said the Volvo car business in China was slow and Swire was not making any money selling cars on the mainland. "It is a long term haul but as you know we are that kind of organisation, we are prepared to take the long haul," said Sutch.

Swire Pacific has been a Volvo distributor in northern and eastern China since 1993 and its Taikoo Motors Ltd unit agreed to acquire the distributorship of Volvo automobiles in Hong Kong and southern and central China earlier this month.
"We would hope to be breaking even on this investment that we have just made in the third year," said Sutch.
